references.text: Moses sent young Israelite men to offer burnt offerings and peace offerings (shelamim) to the Lord, showing the same sacrificial practice with fellowship offerings.
The introduction to the laws concerning peace offerings (shelamim), which is the same type of offering mentioned in Deuteronomy 27:7.
Detailed instructions on the peace offering and how the meat should be eaten, complementing the understanding of the meal mentioned in the verse.
Israel shall eat before the Lord's face and rejoice over all they do, the same combination of a meal and joy before the Lord's presence.
The command to rejoice before the Lord your God with the same expression as in Deuteronomy 27:7.
Instruction to eat before the Lord's face and rejoice, a parallel formulation about a cultic meal and joy.
Instruction to eat before the Lord's face and rejoice with one's household, the same theme of joy in God's presence.
Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal and offers burnt offerings and peace offerings, fulfilling the command from Deuteronomy 27.
